k: Bone claws that spring from a boy's knuckles
Claws and a skeleton laced with adamantium
st: In 1845, young James's bone claws first burst out when his father is murdered, and he kills the killer with them.
Stryker bonds adamantium to Logan's bones and claws, then shoots him with adamantium bullets that wipe his memory.
Waking from a nightmare, Logan stabs Rogue with his claws, and she heals only by absorbing his power.
In the smelting lab where his skeleton was made, Logan fights Stryker's adamantium-clawed Yuriko and kills her.
His adamantium and healing let Logan walk through the Phoenix's fury on Alcatraz, and he stabs Jean.
The Silver Samurai severs his adamantium claws, Mariko stabs Yashida with them, and Logan's bone claws grow back.
Sent back to 1973, Logan finds his claws are bone again; he wakes in a new 2023 where the X-Men live.
In 1983, Stryker keeps an adamantium-clawed Weapon X caged at Alkali Lake until Jean sets him loose.
In 2029, the adamantium slowly poisons Logan; after X-24 impales him, he dies and Laura buries him.
Deadpool digs up Logan's adamantium skeleton and swings it at the TVA agents who come for him.

k: A single bullet Logan keeps for himself
st: Logan has kept one adamantium bullet since escaping Weapon X, once meant for himself; Laura finds it.
Laura loads it into Logan's revolver and shoots X-24 in the head, killing him.

k: Military tags reading Logan and Wolverine
st: Robbed of his memory, Logan finds his dog tags read Logan on one side and Wolverine on the other.
Leaving to look for his past, Logan hands Rogue his dog tags and says he'll be back for them.

k: Xavier's machine for finding any mutant
st: Hank's mutant-locating device, Cerebro, lets Charles find and recruit young mutants for the CIA.
Mystique sabotages Cerebro and it drops Xavier into a coma; Jean uses it to learn Magneto's target, and Xavier recovers.
Xavier uses Cerebro to track Nightcrawler after the attack on the White House.
In 1973, a recovering Charles uses Cerebro again to find Raven before she kills Trask.
En Sabah Nur reaches into Cerebro through Charles and forces the world's nuclear arsenals to launch into space.
Alex blasts Cerebro apart to break En Sabah Nur's hold, and the mansion is destroyed soon after.
In 1992, Charles guides the X-Men's rescue of the shuttle Endeavour from inside a rebuilt Cerebro.
Charles steps down as dean, and Hank takes over the school, renamed for Jean Grey.

k: A second Cerebro, built to kill every mutant
st: Stryker builds a second Cerebro under Alkali Lake and forces a mind-controlled Xavier to aim it at every mutant.
Magneto turns it on humans instead; Storm's snowstorm frees Xavier before the bursting dam floods the base.
Wearing a helmet that blocks telepathy, Shaw follows the Soviet fleet to Cuba in his submarine.
Erik tears it off Shaw so Charles can freeze him, then puts it on himself as he leaves as Magneto.
Magneto wears it so Xavier cannot reach his mind as he plots to mutate the world's leaders.
Subdued at the Statue of Liberty, Magneto ends up in a plastic prison, without his helmet.
Free from his plastic prison, Magneto wears it at Alkali Lake while he turns Stryker's Cerebro on humans.
Magneto wears it as he leads the Brotherhood against the cure and its source on Alcatraz.
In 1973, Magneto retrieves his helmet to shut Charles out, then turns Trask's Sentinels on the White House.

k: A Nazi-decorated coin from Shaw's desk
st: In 1944, Schmidt tells young Erik to move a Nazi coin with his mind; when he can't, Schmidt kills his mother.
Schmidt gives Erik the coin; in 1962, Erik slowly forces it through Shaw's head while Charles holds Shaw frozen.

k: A cure Hank brews from Raven's DNA
st: Hank makes a cure from Raven's DNA; she refuses it, and when he uses it, it turns him blue and furry.
In 1973, Hank's serum lets the broken Charles walk, at the cost of his telepathy.
Charles gives up the serum to get his telepathy back, while Hank keeps taking it to look human.

k: A jet Hank flies for the young mutants
st: Hank pilots his jet, carrying the team and Moira to the Cuban blockade.
Riptide's whirlwind brings the jet down on the beach.
Shaw shadows the Soviet fleet in his submarine to make sure the missiles reach Cuba.
Erik lifts the submarine out of the sea and drops it on the Cuban beach.

k: The X-Men's jet, hidden under the school
st: The X-Jet carries the team to Liberty Island to stop Magneto's machine.
Fighter jets shoot it down and Magneto catches it; at Alkali Lake, Jean lifts it clear of the flood.
The X-Jet flies the team to Alcatraz to fight Magneto's army.

k: A jet Hank has quietly built
st: Hank's jet carries the team to Cairo, where they rescue Charles and take off again.
Angel and Psylocke attack the jet, and it crashes, killing Angel.
Back in service, the X-Jet flies the team into orbit to rescue the crew of the shuttle Endeavour.

k: The lenses that hold back Scott's eye blasts
st: Behind his visor, Cyclops lets loose a blast that knocks out Magneto at the Statue of Liberty.
Brainwashed by Stryker, Scott turns his blasts on Jean at Alkali Lake until their fight frees him.
At Alkali Lake, Jean kills Scott; Logan and Storm find only his glasses and bring them home.
The Phoenix destroys Scott's glasses at the mansion and escapes.

k: A machine that forces mutation on humans
st: Magneto tests his mutation machine on Senator Kelly, whose body later rejects the change and dissolves.
Powered by Rogue atop the Statue of Liberty, it starts to work until Logan destroys it.

k: A shot that suppresses the X-gene
st: Worthington Labs makes a cure from young Jimmy's genome and offers it to any mutant who wants it.
A cure dart meant for Magneto strips Mystique's powers; on Alcatraz, Hank injects Magneto with it.
Rogue takes the cure; in a park, Magneto makes a chess piece wobble.
In a dark 2023, Sentinels built with Mystique's DNA hunt mutants and the humans who protect them.
In 1973, Magneto laces Trask's prototypes with steel and turns them on the White House.
Raven spares Trask, the program is shut down, and the Sentinel future never happens.
Hank and Raven train the new X-Men against confiscated Sentinels.
Dr. Green shows the captive Logan the Silver Samurai, a mechanical suit with energized adamantium katanas.
It severs Logan's adamantium claws and drains his healing, and its pilot is revealed: Yashida.
Mariko stabs Yashida with Logan's severed claws, and Logan throws him off a platform.

k: A device on Logan's heart that slows his healing
st: Dr. Green plants a robotic parasite on Logan's heart while he sleeps, and his wounds stop healing.
Yashida's X-ray machine shows it; Logan cuts himself open and pulls it out.

k: Vials of blood taken from Weapon X
st: After the credits, vials of Weapon X's blood are packed into an Essex Corporation briefcase.

k: The limo Logan drives for hire
st: Logan drives the limo for hire in El Paso; Laura stows away in it, and they escape Pierce's Reavers.
Logan ditches the bullet-riddled limo at a junkyard and buys a used pickup truck.

k: Comic books that mark the way to Eden
st: Logan finds Eden in Laura's X-Men comic and calls it fiction, but she will not give up on reaching it.

k: A serum that boosts healing for a time
st: Logan takes an overdose of the serum Rictor gave him and fights off the Reavers until it wears off.

k: Twin swords worn on Deadpool's back
st: Deadpool carves through Ajax's convoy on the expressway with his twin katanas.
Deadpool keeps them strapped to his back as he hunts crime bosses and forms X-Force.
Pulled into the Void, Deadpool fights Cassandra Nova's forces with his katanas.

k: A red suit so foes can't see him bleed
st: Wade makes himself a red suit, so the bad guys won't see him bleed, and becomes Deadpool.
Cable straps Vanessa's token inside the suit over Wade's heart, where it stops a bullet.
Wade puts the suit back on to save his universe from the TVA.
After Vanessa dies, a Skee-Ball token, her anniversary gift, is all Wade has left of her.
Cable takes the token from Wade when he storms the Ice Box.
Cable goes back minutes in time and straps it over Wade's heart, where it stops the bullet meant for Russell.

k: A wrist device that travels through time
st: Cable comes from the future to kill Russell, then spends its last charge going back to save Wade.
Negasonic and Yukio repair it, and Wade uses it to save Vanessa and Peter.
Wade and Russell are fitted with power-suppressing collars and locked in the Ice Box.
Wearing an Ice Box collar, Wade leaps in front of Cable's bullet for Russell and dies.

k: A decommissioned Helicarrier in a scrapyard
st: Ajax holds Vanessa on a decommissioned Helicarrier in a scrapyard.
Negasonic blasts away its supports, and it collapses while Deadpool shields Vanessa.
Dopinder drives Deadpool in his taxi on the way to the expressway ambush.
Dopinder runs over the orphanage headmaster with his taxi.
Illyana keeps a dragon puppet named Lockheed, and brings back a small living Lockheed to fight the Demon Bear.

k: A glowing sword from Illyana's special place
st: Illyana travels to her special place and returns with a glowing sword and armor to fight the Demon Bear.
In season 2, a flashback shows Cornelius lacing Wolverine's bones with adamantium; Alpha Flight later plans to extract it.
In season 1, Wolverine stabs Magneto on Asteroid M, and Magneto rips every bit of adamantium out of his skeleton.
In season 2, Wolverine finds a Weapon X facility and its adamantium process gives him back his adamantium claws.

k: The machine that amplifies psychic power
st: In season 2, Jean uses Cerebro to search for the missing Professor and to merge the warring minds inside Rogue.
In season 3, Xavier picks up a telepathic signal from an alien prison ship with Cerebro.
In season 1, Jean uses Cerebro to probe Gyrich's mind in prison and find Bolivar Trask.
In season 1, Sentinels hunt Jubilee at a mall, and the X-Men raid the program's mutant database.
In season 1, Sentinels massacre Genosha, and Bastion turns humans into Prime Sentinels to attack mutants worldwide.
In season 1, Jean's collar cuts Bastion off from his Sentinels and frees the Prime Sentinels, and missiles kill him.

k: The giant machine that builds Sentinels
st: In season 1, Master Mold turns on its makers; Xavier flies the Blackbird into it and it explodes.
In season 1, an upgraded Master Mold leads the attack on Genosha, and Gambit dies destroying it.
In season 1, Xavier flies the Blackbird, packed with explosives and shielded by Magneto, into Master Mold.
In season 2, the X-Men fly a Blackbird again, to the Savage Land to rescue Xavier.
In season 1, the X-Men take the Blackbird to a Sahara junkyard to find Bolivar Trask.

k: The helmet that shields Magneto's mind
st: In season 1, Magneto, in his helmet, seizes a military base's missiles until the X-Men stop him.
In season 2, Apocalypse vaporizes Magneto in ancient Egypt, and only his helmet is left for Xavier to hold.

k: Cards Gambit charges with kinetic energy
st: In season 1, Gambit fights beside the X-Men with his charged playing cards.
In season 1, Gambit dies destroying Master Mold; Apocalypse later finds one of his cards in Genosha.
In season 2, X-Force finds one of Gambit's cards beside Apocalypse's corpse in Athens.

k: An ancient Shi'ar crystal of cosmic power
st: In season 3, Lilandra steals the M'Kraan Crystal from her brother D'Ken and seeks out Xavier.
In season 3, D'Ken seizes the crystal and, drawn inside it, sets out to remake the universe.
In season 3, Phoenix destroys D'Ken's mind and takes the crystal to the Sun, where no one can reach it again.
In season 4, Magneto offers all mutants a peaceful, human-free life on his orbiting Asteroid M.
In season 4, Fabian Cortez tricks Magneto into an escape pod, takes Asteroid M and fires missiles at Earth.
In season 4, Magneto returns in time to destroy both the missiles and Asteroid M.
In season 1, Magneto re-establishes his mutant haven on a new Asteroid M, leaving Earth without power.
In season 1, Bastion tries to crash Asteroid M into Earth.
In season 1, missiles kill Bastion, and Magneto sends the falling asteroid into space, where it explodes.
In season 2, in 3000 B.C., the X-Men find the Ship, and through it En Sabah Nur becomes Apocalypse.
In season 3, Beast boards Apocalypse's sentient ship and turns it on him; Apocalypse sets it to self-destruct, and it sinks.
In season 2, Beast, Rogue and Nightcrawler find the Ship abandoned by Apocalypse, and Rogue speaks with Eson through it.

k: A collar that blocks Bastion's technopathy
st: In season 1, Beast and Forge build a collar that can block Bastion's control of his Sentinels.
In season 1, Jean puts the collar on Bastion, then he dies on Asteroid M, which explodes in space.
In season 2, Rogue traps Apocalypse's consciousness in a crystal and gives it to Cable.
In season 5, Gyrich attacks Xavier with an energy disruptor at a summit, leaving him dying.

k: A promised cure for mutant powers
st: In season 1, Dr. Adler's cure on Muir Island is run by Mystique in disguise, as a trap for Apocalypse.
In season 1, the machine turns cure seekers into Apocalypse's Horsemen until Rogue destroys it.

k: Blade's sword, with a booby-trapped hilt
st: Blade cuts through Frost's vampires with it; its hilt springs blades into any hand that grabs it unprepared.
Beaten by Blade, the Reaper Nomak takes Blade's sword and kills himself with it.
Blade duels Drake with his sword until Drake bests him, and only the Daystar arrow ends the fight.
In the Void, Blade fights Cassandra Nova's army with it.

k: A folding silver blade that flies back to Blade
st: Blade throws his folding silver glaive at vampires and it returns to his hand.
Blade carries a new glaive as he hunts vampires in Prague.

k: A shot that holds back Blade's thirst
st: Whistler's serum holds back Blade's thirst but is losing its power; Karen sets out to improve it.
Shen now makes the serum, and Blade injects Krista with it to tame her new vampire hunger.

k: An anticoagulant that makes vampire blood explode
st: Testing EDTA as a new serum, Karen finds it makes vampire blood explode.
Blade injects Frost with syringes of EDTA, and Frost swells up and bursts.

k: The holy book of the vampires
st: Pages of the Book of Erebus sit in Pearl's vampire archive; Pearl reveals Frost's plan to raise La Magra.

k: A charge Blade fixes to Reinhardt's skull
st: Blade fixes an explosive to the back of Reinhardt's skull to keep him in line.
Scud thinks it a dud, but Blade swapped in a live charge and kills Scud with it.

k: A bomb that floods the dark with sunlight
st: Whistler and Scud build a UV bomb for Blade to take into the Reapers' nest.
Blade sets it off in the nest, killing every Reaper but Nomak.

k: A virus made to kill vampires
st: The Nightstalkers' scientist Sommerfield makes Daystar, a virus that needs Drake's blood to work.
Blade stabs Drake with the Daystar arrow, and the finished virus spreads through the air, killing the vampires.

k: A vaccine to free vampires from their weaknesses
st: Marcus's Aurora vaccine makes Fritz immune to sunlight, silver and garlic.
Aurora is really a virus that kills purebloods, and Marcus unleashes it with Blade's help.

k: A weapon disguised as a white cane
st: Matt fights crime with a weaponized baton that he disguises as his white cane.
Bullseye steals the baton and impales Nikolas Natchios with it, leaving it behind to frame Daredevil.
Believing Daredevil killed her father, Elektra stabs him with her sai, then learns he is Matt.
Bullseye kills Elektra with one of her own sai.
Brought back to life, Elektra kills Typhoid with her sai after Typhoid poisons Abby.
In the Void, Elektra fights Cassandra Nova's forces with her sai.

k: A necklace with Elektra's name in braille
st: Matt finds Elektra's necklace, her name in braille, on the roof where they first kissed.

k: A black shirt with a white skull
st: Frank's son Will buys him a skull shirt, told it protects against evil spirits.
Frank wears his son's gift as he wages war on Howard Saint's family.
Frank kills the hitman Harry Heck on a bridge and takes his car as a prize.
Frank plants Livia's earring in Glass's bed; Howard Saint finds it and stabs Glass to death.

k: A machine to recreate the cosmic storm
st: Reed builds a machine to recreate the storm and undo their powers, but cannot power it.
Victor powers it with his own electricity and turns Ben human again.
Ben climbs back in and turns himself into the Thing to save Reed.
Ben tells Reed to forget the machine; he has made peace with who he is.

k: The source of the Silver Surfer's power
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
st: A silver alien rides a flying board around the Earth, leaving craters, and overpowers Johnny.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Reed's pulse cuts the Surfer off from his board, and the military takes them both.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Doom steals the board and rides it to Shanghai.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Johnny and Ben knock Doom off it; the Surfer rides it into Galactus, and a blast engulfs them both.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Drifting in space, the Surfer opens his eyes and his board flies back to him.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A device to cut the Surfer off from his board
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
st: In the Black Forest, Reed's pulse generator separates the Surfer from his board.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
st: The Four free the Surfer and chase Doom to Shanghai in the Fantasticar.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: The mist that unlocks Inhuman powers
st: Iridia and Bronaja are exposed to the Terrigen Mist in a ceremony on Attilan to reveal their powers.
Karnak uses a second Terrigenesis, with Auran's DNA, to bring Gorgon back.
Medusa entrusts the Terrigen crystals to Louise on Earth, out of Maximus's reach.

k: A device that keeps Attilan stable
st: Maximus reveals a failsafe that needs his fingerprints every hour to keep Attilan stable.

k: A magic staff that answers to the Minorus
st: In season 1, Nico uses her mother Tina's staff to find Alex; it stays at the Minoru house when she runs.
In season 2, Nico takes the staff back from Tina, then buries it, afraid of its power.
Jonah finds the staff Nico buried and breaks it.
Nico summons the Staff of One again and makes Jonah and his family disappear.
In season 1, Chase builds the Fistigons; his father Victor attacks him with them and is shot.
In season 2, a biker steals the Fistigons from Chase, and the Runaways get them back.
In season 1, Karolina takes off her Church of Gibborim bracelet at a party, and her hands begin to glow.
In season 2, Jonah teaches Karolina to use her powers without the bracelet.

k: Strange rocks from the Hernandez home
st: In season 1, young Molly survives the fire that kills her parents because she is holding strange glowing rocks.
In season 2, Topher, who saw the Hernandezes die, is hooked on their rocks.

k: The alien ship buried under Los Angeles
st: In season 2, Jonah reveals he is digging up his ship to go home, and the Pride blows it up.
Jonah's family builds a new ship, which needs all four of them to power it.
Nico makes Jonah and his family vanish with the Staff of One.
Robert records pages of Morgan's grimoire, the Darkhold, with his glasses, before Morgan kills him.
WIZARD's free Corvus phones turn people violent, and Morgan plans to build an army with them.
Janet knocks out the Los Angeles phone service, and Tina banishes Morgan to the Dark Dimension.

k: A Mardi Gras cloak Billy began
st: In season 1, Tyrone finishes the cloak his late brother Billy began, and Connors is swallowed by its darkness.

k: Proof hidden in a safety deposit box
st: In season 1, Tandy gets the evidence her father Nathan hid in a safety deposit box to clear his name.
In season 1, Tandy confronts Roxxon's Scarborough with her father's hidden evidence, then takes his bribe for it.
In season 2, Andre drains people's despair and keeps it as records in a dreamlike record store.
In season 2, Mayhem destroys the records so that Tyrone can rescue Tandy.
